title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Provisions on the Management of Execution Funds and Property
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Provisions on the Management of Execution Funds and Property

Fa Fa [2017] No. 6

To: High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the PLA Military Court; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

In order to standardize the management of execution funds and property by people's courts and to protect the lawful rights and interests of parties, the Supreme People's Court has revised the Provisions on the Management of Execution Funds and Property (for Trial Implementation) (Fa Fa [2006] No. 11) promulgated and implemented on May 18, 2006. The revised Provisions on the Management of Execution Funds and Property of the Supreme People's Court are hereby issued for your compliance and implementation.

February 27, 2017

Provisions on the Management of Execution Funds and Property

In order to standardize the management of execution funds and property by people's courts and to protect the lawful rights and interests of parties, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and relevant judicial interpretations, with reference to relevant financial management regulations, and in light of the actual work of enforcement.

Article 1 For the purposes of these Provisions, "execution funds and property" refers to funds and property that, according to law, shall be under the management and control of the people's court during the execution proceedings.

Article 2 The management of execution funds and property shall follow the principle of division of responsibilities, mutual cooperation, and mutual supervision between the enforcement organ and the relevant management departments.

Article 3 The finance department shall register the receipt and payment of execution funds on a case-by-case basis and establish detailed accounts.

For sealed-up or seized items stored by the people's court, a designated person or department shall be assigned to register them on a case-by-case basis, keep them in safe custody, and no one may use them without authorization.

The enforcement organ shall designate a specific person to manage the receipt and distribution of execution funds and property, establish ledgers, register on a case-by-case basis, and conduct a monthly reconciliation with the management department of execution funds and property regarding the receipt and distribution.

Article 4 People's courts shall open a special account for execution funds or set up an execution funds category within the special account for case funds, and carry out special management, independent accounting, and dedicated payment of execution funds.

People's courts shall adopt a "one account per case" approach to centrally manage execution funds, ensuring a one-to-one correspondence between the case number, the funds, and the judgment debtor or payer.

Article 5 Enforcement personnel shall, in the notice of enforcement or relevant legal documents, inform the parties of the name of the bank where the special account for execution funds or the special account for case funds is opened, the account number, the account name, and the information to be noted when making a payment, including the enforcement case number, the name of the judgment debtor, the name of the payer, and the purpose of the payment.

Article 6 A judgment debtor may directly pay execution funds to the judgment creditor; the people's court may also directly transfer execution funds from the judgment debtor's account to the judgment creditor's account. However, execution funds that are disputed or need to be redistributed, as well as execution funds that the people's court deems truly necessary, shall be transferred to the special account for execution funds or the special account for case funds.

Execution funds deducted and transferred by the people's court through the online enforcement inquiry and control system shall be transferred to the special account for execution funds or the special account for case funds.

Article 7 Where a payer directly delivers execution funds to the people's court, enforcement personnel may, together with the payer, or the payer may directly, go to the finance department to handle the relevant procedures.

If cash is delivered, the finance department shall immediately issue a receipt voucher to the payer; if a negotiable instrument is delivered, the finance department shall immediately issue a collection voucher to the payer, and shall notify the enforcement personnel to collect the receipt voucher within three days after the funds are credited to the account.

After receiving the receipt voucher from the finance department, enforcement personnel shall promptly notify the judgment debtor or payer to exchange the collection voucher for the receipt voucher within a specified period. If the judgment debtor or payer fails to complete the exchange procedure within the specified period or expressly refuses to do so, the enforcement personnel shall state the reasons in writing and attach it, together with the receipt voucher, to the case file.

Article 8 Where a payer delivers execution funds by bank transfer or remittance, or where the people's court collects execution funds by deduction and transfer, the finance department shall notify the enforcement personnel to collect the receipt voucher within three days after the funds are credited to the account.

After receiving the receipt voucher from the finance department, enforcement personnel shall handle the matter with reference to the provisions of paragraph 3 of Article 7 of these Provisions.

Article 9 In principle, enforcement personnel shall not directly accept cash or negotiable instruments; if direct acceptance is truly necessary, there shall be no fewer than two enforcement personnel present, and they shall immediately issue a collection voucher to the payer, while also making a collection record, which shall be signed by the payer and the persons present.

If enforcement personnel directly accept cash or negotiable instruments, they shall transfer the cash or negotiable instruments to the finance department on the same day after returning to the court; if it is truly difficult to do so on the same day, they shall transfer them within one day after returning to the court and explain the reasons. The finance department shall handle the matter in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 7 of these Provisions.

After receiving the receipt voucher from the finance department, enforcement personnel shall handle the matter in accordance with paragraph 3 of Article 7 of these Provisions.

Article 10 Enforcement personnel shall, within thirty days from the date of receiving the notice from the finance department that the execution funds have been credited, complete the accounting of the execution funds, the settlement of enforcement costs, the notification of the judgment creditor to collect, and the disbursement of the execution funds.

Disbursement may be delayed with the approval of the head of the enforcement bureau or the responsible court leader under any of the following circumstances:

(1) Apportionment of case funds is required;
(2) The execution funds are preserved or frozen due to the judgment creditor being involved in another lawsuit, enforcement, or suspected criminal activities;
(3) The judgment creditor has been notified but has not collected;
(4) The case is lawfully suspended or the enforcement is temporarily stayed;
(5) Other legitimate reasons exist for delaying the disbursement of execution funds.

After the above circumstances cease to exist, enforcement personnel shall complete the disbursement of the execution funds within ten days.

Article 11 When a people's court disburses execution funds, it shall generally adopt the method of bank transfer.

Execution funds shall be disbursed to the judgment creditor; if it is truly necessary to disburse them to a unit or individual other than the judgment creditor, a collegial panel shall be formed to review the case, except where the funds are to be returned to the payer according to law.

Article 12 When disbursing execution funds, enforcement personnel shall fill out an approval form for the disbursement of execution funds. The approval form shall specify the enforcement case number, the names of the parties, the name of the payer, the amount paid, the time of payment, the method of payment, the name of the payee, the payee's account number, the amount to be disbursed, and the method of disbursement. After obtaining approval from the head of the enforcement bureau or the responsible court leader, it shall be submitted to the finance department for handling the payment procedures.

If another person is authorized to handle the procedures for collecting execution funds, a special power of attorney and a copy of the authorized agent's identity card shall be attached. If the authorized agent is a lawyer, a formal letter issued by the law firm and a copy of the lawyer's license shall be attached.

Article 13 If the judgment creditor requests or agrees that the people's court disburses execution funds by bank transfer, the enforcement personnel shall submit the approval form for the disbursement of execution funds and the written certification of the account information provided by the judgment creditor for receiving the execution funds to the finance department to handle the transfer procedures.

If the judgment creditor or its authorized agent comes directly to the people's court to handle the procedures for collecting execution funds, the enforcement personnel shall, after verifying the identity document and the authorization documents of the person collecting the funds, hold the approval form for the disbursement of execution funds and go together with the person collecting the funds to the finance department to handle the payment procedures.

Article 14 When the finance department handles the payment procedures for execution funds, it shall not only verify the approval form for the disbursement of execution funds but also conduct a review in accordance with relevant financial management regulations.

Article 15 When disbursing execution funds, the payee shall issue a lawful and valid receipt voucher. If the finance department has other provisions, those shall prevail.

Article 16 If execution funds cannot be disbursed within the prescribed period due to any of the following circumstances, the people's court may lodge the execution funds:

(1) The judgment creditor refuses to collect without legitimate reason;
(2) The whereabouts of the judgment creditor are unknown;
(3) The judgment creditor has died and no heir has been determined, or has lost capacity for civil conduct and no guardian has been determined;
(4) The judgment creditor cannot be notified to collect through the contact information provided;
(5) Other circumstances where disbursement cannot be made.

Article 17 If execution funds need to be lodged, enforcement personnel shall fill out an approval form for the lodgment of execution funds and attach evidence of the circumstances giving rise to the lodgment. The approval form for the lodgment of execution funds shall specify the enforcement case number, the names of the parties, the name of the payer, the amount paid, the time of payment, the method of payment, the name of the payee, the amount to be lodged, and the reasons for lodgment. After obtaining approval from the head of the enforcement bureau or the responsible court leader, the lodgment procedures shall be handled.

The costs of lodgment shall be borne by the judgment creditor and may be deducted from the execution funds.

Article 18 If a judgment debtor directly delivers to the judgment creditor the items (including negotiable instruments, certificates, licenses, etc.) required to be delivered or returned under the enforcement basis, the judgment debtor shall provide the people's court with proof of receipt of the items; if there is no proof of receipt, the enforcement personnel shall record the performance in the record, which shall be attached to the case file after being signed by both parties.

If a judgment debtor delivers items to the people's court for forwarding to the judgment creditor, or if the people's court presides over the delivery between the parties, the enforcement personnel shall record the delivery in the record, which shall be attached to the case file after being signed by both parties.

Article 19 For items sealed up or seized to the people's court, or items directly delivered to the people's court by the judgment debtor, a surety, or others, enforcement personnel shall immediately notify the custody department to inventory and register the items. Valuable items such as negotiable securities, gold, silver, jewelry, and antiques shall be sealed and stored, and a handover shall be conducted. After receiving the items, the custody department shall issue a collection voucher.

For items sealed up or seized in another location that are inconvenient to transport or easily damaged, the people's court may entrust the people's court at the location of the items to keep them in custody, and the entrusted people's court shall handle the matter in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 20 People's courts shall designate a specific location for storing the items referred to in Article 19 of these Provisions.

Article 21 For seasonal goods, fresh goods, perishable goods, and other items unsuitable for long-term storage, the people's court may order the parties to dispose of them promptly and deliver the proceeds to the people's court; if necessary, enforcement personnel may sell them, and deliver the proceeds to the finance department in accordance with the requirements of these Provisions.

Article 22 For items sealed up or seized by the people's court, or delivered by the judgment debtor, which are required to be delivered or returned under the enforcement basis, enforcement personnel shall, within thirty days from the date of sealing up, seizing, or delivery by the judgment debtor, complete the settlement of enforcement costs, notify the judgment creditor to collect, and disburse the items. For items not required to be delivered or returned under the enforcement basis, if the conditions for disposal are met, enforcement personnel shall initiate the property disposal procedure according to law.

Article 23 When the people's court lifts the sealing up or seizure of items, except where the items are kept in custody by the judgment debtor, the items shall be returned to the owner or the deliverer within ten days from the date of lifting the sealing up or seizure.

Losses caused by natural wear and tear or depreciation of items during the period of sealing up or seizure by the people's court shall be borne by the owner or the deliverer, unless otherwise provided by law.

Article 24 If any of the circumstances specified in Article 16 of these Provisions exist, the people's court may lodge the items.

If the items are unsuitable for lodgment or the lodgment costs are excessive, the people's court may lodge the proceeds from the auction or sale of the items.

Article 25 The disbursement, delayed disbursement, and lodgment of items shall, unless otherwise expressly provided in these Provisions, be handled with reference to the relevant provisions on execution funds.

Article 26 Receipt vouchers and relevant evidentiary materials for execution funds and property shall be attached to the case file for archiving.

Article 27 When the case handler is transferred away from the enforcement organ, at the time of handing over the case, the receipt vouchers and related materials for execution funds and property must also be handed over. If the receipt and distribution of execution funds and property are complex, an audit may be conducted at the time of handover. If the handover of execution funds and property is not clear, the transfer procedures shall not be processed.

Article 28 In implementing these Provisions, each High People's Court may formulate specific implementation measures in light of the requirements of building internal controls in administrative institutions and the actual work of enforcement.

Article 29 These Provisions shall take effect as of May 1, 2017. The Provisions on the Management of Execution Funds and Property (for Trial Implementation) (Fa Fa [2006] No. 11) of the Supreme People's Court, which were implemented on May 18, 2006, shall be simultaneously abrogated.
